chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) would insure the tailor and the goldsmith out of precaution, and my father (peace be upon him) would extend the period (of credit) for them if they were trustworthy.

key_terms.اَلصَّائِغَ: The goldsmith (one who works with gold)
key_terms.اَلْقَصَّارَ: The tailor (one who cuts and sews cloth)
key_terms.اِحْتِيَاطاً: Out of precaution (fiqh term for precautionary measure)
key_terms.يَتَطَوَّلُ: He extended (the period of credit or delay)
key_terms.يُضَمِّنُ: He insured or guaranteed (the debt/work of another)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between insuring (itminan) and extending credit (tatawwul) in Shia commercial jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the pragmatic application of commercial risk management in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the precautionary guarantee (*daman*) employed by Imam Ali (AS) and the credit extension (*tatawwul*) favored by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) based on the artisan's trustworthiness. It underscores the scholarly principle that financial arrangements in trade should be tailored to the specific reliability (*ma'muniyyah*) of the party involved, balancing security with economic facilitation. This distinction remains a key reference in *fiqh al-mu'amalat* for determining when to impose strict liability versus when to allow deferred payment based on reputation.
